question: Reports published1 in the Bulgarian media have raised serious misgivings over the allocation of funding for cultural schemes financed through the Bulgarian Recovery and Resilience Plan.

It has been broadly disclosed that several projects connected with the same person received funding through different companies, that the amounts approved or advanced for these projects significantly exceeded well-established industry practices, and that some of these decisions were taken during the latter days of the previous government. The Bulgarian authorities have since begun conducting checks2.

Given that Article 22 of Regulation (EU) 2021/241 requires Member States to protect the financial interests of the Union and to take appropriate measures to prevent, detect and correct fraud, corruption, conflicts of interests and double funding, would the Commission please specify: 1.
Whether it has requested clarifications from the Bulgarian authorities on these procedures and the funding granted under them?
Whether similar suspicions of irregularities have arisen regarding other projects under the same procedures or under other schemes financed through the RRP in Bulgaria?

Whether it considers that Bulgaria’s control mechanisms under the RRP provide sufficient guarantees to ensure quality management of funding and whether it intends to take further action in response to signs of weak controls, irregularities and lack of transparency?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (15.6.2026) The Recovery and Resilience Facility (RRF) is a performance-based instrument, where the Commission assesses the satisfactory fulfilment of milestones and targets linked to measures included in Member States’ Recovery and Resilience Plans according to the requirements of the related Council Implementing Decision.

With regards to the individual projects referred to in the question, the Commission would like to clarify that as the investment is part of the fourth payment request, which is currently under assessment by the Commission, the Commission is not in position to confirm the final list of projects funded under the RRF.

The Commission has been informed by the Bulgarian authorities about the ongoing internal checks related to certain projects pertaining to this investment. Member States are responsible for the implementation of measures supported by the RRF and must protect the EU financial interests and ensure that the use of funds complies with the applicable EU and national rules1.

Member States shall provide an effective and efficient internal control system. The Commission evaluated the control system set out by Bulgaria in its assessment of the RRP, as reflected in the Council Implementing Decision, concluding that the arrangements are adequate to prevent, detect and correct corruption, fraud and conflicts of interest, as well as to avoid double funding.
A subsequent system audit performed by Commission services supports this overall assessment.
1 European Parliament and Council. 2021. Regulation (EU) 2021/241 on the establishment of the Recovery and
Resilience Facility, February 12, Article 22(1) (‘RRF Regulation’), available at https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legalcontent/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=CELEX:32021R0241.
